speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe your specific gait difficulties and any limb coordination issues you are experiencing. Additionally, could you outline your significant medical history in detail?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing those symptoms; the "drunken" gait and right-sided clumsiness strongly suggest cerebellar involvement. Given your significant medical history, are you currently taking any immunosuppressive medications or have you received recent chemotherapy or radiation therapy? Also, have you noticed any changes in your vision or balance when lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The combination of subacute cerebellar ataxia, a known side effect of this drug, and your history of Crohn's disease makes this the most likely diagnosis. I am requesting MRI images of your brain to confirm the presence of non-enhancing white matter lesions typical of PML.
